# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

content.text:
So the harness serves a static `index.html` at root (no package.json). I should build a pure HTML/CSS/JS game (maybe with modules) — no build step needed. Static files served from root.

The concept: "DON'T LOOK BACK" — monster moves only when you're not looking. Longer you stare = reality breaks. This maps really well to a first-person game with a "blink/gaze" mechanic.

Design considerations:
- Must run in browser, mobile + desktop, responsive, touch controls.
- Should be visually impressive: I'll build a first-person raycaster-style 3D corridor game using Canvas 2D raycaster with custom shaders? Or Three.js? Three.js would need CDN or vendored file. CDN may be blocked? Network likely available but a self-contained static is safest. A raycaster in Canvas 2D can look atmospheric with limited effort: fog, textured walls, flashlight, sprites.

Actually, could do a custom WebGL renderer for a 3D corridor with SDF-ish visuals. But a raycaster with procedural textures can be very moody and is reliable. Alternative: a "corridor walker" with perspective-projected sprites and pre-rendered environment layers — simpler pseudo-3D.

Let me think about what makes the mechanic fun and legible:

Core loop: You're in a dark corridor/labyrinth. The monster ("The Watcher") is behind/around you. It only moves when it's not in your view. You must look at it to freeze it. But staring drains "sanity" / breaks reality: vignette distorts, colors invert, walls breathe, whispers, false monsters, geometry warps, UI glitches. If you look away too long, it advances and kills you. You need to reach an exit by walking backward? Interesting twist: "Don't look back" — the title suggests you should NOT look. But monster moves when not looked at... Hmm title "DON'T LOOK BACK" implies the danger is looking back? Wait: monster moves only when you're not looking at it. So looking back freezes it. But staring breaks reality. The title is a trap: the game encourages you to look back, and that's what breaks you.

Maybe a better loop: the monster approaches from behind. You hear it. To survive you must turn and look (freezing it), but every second of gaze increases "Break" meter. At max break, reality fractures and something worse happens. You must balance: look briefly, then move. When you turn away it advances. Reach the exit.

Mechanics:
- Move forward/back/strafe (WASD / touch joystick).
- Turn (mouse / drag / arrow keys).
- Gaze meter fills while monster is on screen; when full, "reality break" phase triggers — visuals, monster teleports/duplicates, maybe it advances fast for a moment, sanity damage.
- Stamina/blink? Maybe "blink" mechanic: you have to blink periodically and during blink it moves far.

To keep scope achievable and polished, use a 2.5D raycaster with:
- Procedural wall textures generated to canvas (concrete, wallpaper, doors) — can do.
- Floor/ceiling casting or simple gradient + fog.
- Billboard sprite for monster drawn procedurally (a tall thin figure with glowing eyes) with layers; animate sway.
- Dynamic lighting: flashlight cone brightens center, darkness at edges, flicker.
- Screen effects: chromatic aberration approximated via CSS filters / canvas offset draws, vignette, noise, scanlines, warping (sliced draw offsets), text glitches.
- Audio via WebAudio: procedural drone, heartbeat, footsteps, whispers, screech. No external assets needed. Must start on user gesture.
- Touch controls: left virtual joystick for movement, right drag to look; tap buttons maybe sprint. Also gyro optional.
- Fullscreen, pause, restart, intro screen with title and instructions, death screen, win condition.
- Performance: render at reduced internal resolution (e.g. canvas 640x360 scaled up) for speed and pixelated horror aesthetic. Good.
- Mobile safe areas.

Level: a maze/corridor with an exit. Could procedurally generate a small maze and place an exit. But performance and collision easier with grid maze. A raycaster with grid map is ideal. Generate a maze (recursive backtracker) with wide corridors? Standard 1-cell corridors might feel claustrophobic—that's fine. Exit at farthest cell. Monster spawns behind player and pursues when not visible. Add "eyes" pickups? Maybe collect 3 "fuses"/"memories" to open exit — gives objective and exploration. Each pickup triggers a reality-break escalation. Nice structure: 3 sigils, exit gate.

Pacing: The monster always knows your position and moves along maze path toward you? Pathfinding (BFS) on grid each tick. It moves only when not in view. Speed increases with each sigil/with time. When it's very close, breathing gets loud, screen darkens.

Gaze/break:
- gazeHeat increases while monster visible, decays when not. Above threshold, reality distortions begin and intensify. At 100%, "FRACTURE": screen tears, monster lunges a few cells closer, player control inverted briefly, vignette red, loud sound. After fracture, heat resets to ~40%.
- Also give player a "focus/breath" resource? Simpler: staring is the risk. There's a counter "REALITY: 100%" decreasing with gaze. When it hits 0 -> death by "the truth". Hmm.

Let me define:
- VISIBILITY meter: when monster on screen, it's frozen and "ATTENTION" rises. At 100 attention, reality fractures (screen glitch, monster jumps closer, attention drops to 0, reality integrity -1 of 3). Three fractures = death (or reality collapse).
- When not looking, monster advances at speed based on progress.
- Monster catch = death.
- 3 sigils to collect; then exit.

Wait — with monster frozen while looked at, and you must walk to sigils while not looking... you'd walk backward facing the monster (strafe) to keep it frozen. That's a fun and creepy mechanic: move backward while staring. But staring breaks reality. So you alternate. Also, if monster around corner, you see it only when in corridor.

Could add: when you look at it, it "hides" after a couple seconds? Then no point staring. Maybe gaze meter eventually causes it to disappear and reappear closer ("blink"). That's the risk.

Simplify and polish: monster on screen freezes. Attention builds. At threshold fracture: monster vanishes and reappears much closer + reality damage. So staring too long is punished.

Pathfinding: BFS in maze grid to player; it moves along path. It should not enter player's cell (death at distance < 0.6).

Visibility check: monster must be within FOV and line of sight (raycast against walls) and within some distance. Also light? Flashlight always on; make it visible within 14 cells.

Monster rendering as sprite with screen-space position from camera transform. Draw with alpha and scale based on distance; flicker.

Player movement: smooth, with collision against walls, headbob, footsteps audio. Turn via mouse (pointer lock on desktop; drag on touch), joystick for WASD on touch. Also sprint.

Minimap? No—maze should be disorienting. Add compass? Maybe subtle "sigil sense" arrow/direction indicator when close? Horror benefits from no minimap, but finding 3 sigils in a maze could be tedious. Add a faint directional pulse toward nearest sigil triggered by pressing/holding "E"? Or a "heartbeat" that quickens near sigils. Use audio cue. Alternatively make the level linear-ish: a looping corridor with branches. A small maze (15x15) with 3 sigils and clear audio cues is okay.

I think add a "signal" mechanic: hold Space / tap button to "listen" — a faint tone that indicates direction to nearest sigil (also makes noise attracting monster faster briefly). Nice risk/reward, gives player agency.

Amount of work: This is a big single-file game, maybe 1500-2500 lines JS. Let's structure files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- js/audio.js, js/maze.js, js/renderer.js, js/game.js? Or one main.js for simplicity but organized sections. Static server serves any file. Multiple files cleaner.

Need to be careful about browser support: modules (type="module") fine. WebAudio fine. Pointer lock fine.

Raycaster performance: canvas width 480 (internal), each column one ray using DDA. Height 270. Upscale with image-rendering: pixelated? For horror aesthetic, slight pixelation at 2x scale is nice. But text overlay should be crisp HTML. I'll render 3D at ~640x360 and CSS-scale to full, with smoothing off maybe. Add grain/vignette as HTML overlays (CSS gradients), plus glitch via canvas transforms.

Textures: generate 64x64 procedural textures at startup: wall (concrete/stained wallpaper), door, sigil wall, floor, ceiling. Draw walls with texture sampling per column (vertical strips) — need per-pixel sampling; can use drawImage with a 1px-wide slice of texture scaled: ctx.drawImage(tex, texX, 0, 1, texHeight, x, drawStart, 1, drawHeight) — that's fast enough (640 draws/frame). Shading via globalAlpha black overlay per column: draw wall slice then fillRect with rgba black based on distance & side. That's 1280 draw ops per frame, okay at 60fps? On mobile maybe ~30-45fps. Could reduce internal width to 420 and use silhouette style. Let's aim 480x270 internal for mobile, 640x360 desktop? Simple: internal width = min(560, window inner width * 0.5) maybe. Keep adaptive.

Better approach for lighting: use a per-column darkened slice by drawing texture then overlay gradient in screen space (radial flashlight) on top of whole frame — cheaper and looks good: darken edges with radial gradient centered slightly below center, plus distance fog via per-column black fill (needed). We can do per-column shade with one fillRect each — fine.

Floor: simple horizon gradient with perspective grid lines? Add floor casting optional. Raycaster floors can be done with per-row sampling from a floor texture — 480*270/2 = 64k samples in JS per frame → too slow maybe (~4-8ms). Could render floor as gradient with a few moving perspective lines and fog. But a textured floor massively improves 3D feel. Alternative: draw floor as vertical gradient and add perspective lines (tiles) computed cheaply: for rows near horizon lines converge. Simpler: dark floor with subtle radial texture noise overlay and vignette; the corridors are dark anyway.

Actually, I can do floor casting at low internal resolution (480x270), with per-pixel set into ImageData. Walls via DDA written into the same ImageData. Full software renderer: 480*270 = 129,600 pixels; per pixel operations fairly cheap. That could run at 60fps on desktop, maybe 30 on mobile. Floor casting with texture sampling adds cost but manageable. Software renderer gives full control: texture sampling, distance fog, flashlight attenuation, noise, sprite z-buffer, chromatic aberration maybe second pass. Let's build a proper mini-engine:

- Precompute wall textures as Uint32Array (64x64 each) generated procedurally.
- Render into ImageData buffer (Uint32).
- DDA per column for walls; floor/ceiling casting per row.
- Fog/light per pixel: brightness = flashlight(dist, angle) * ambient; apply color.
- Sprite drawing with z-buffer.

## Objective
- Build a browser horror game from the user's concept: “DON'T LOOK BACK — A horror game where the monster moves only when you're not looking at it. But the longer you stare, the more reality starts breaking.”
- Self-contained static web game, desktop + mobile, with atmospheric visuals, audio, and the gaze/reality mechanic.

## Requirements
- User provided only the concept/title; no further explicit constraints.
- Follow repo guidance: responsive mobile support with usable touch controls, gameplay within safe areas, avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Use persistent tmux sessions for long-lived servers; verify with Playwright/SwiftShader screenshots.
- No external assets allowed by current design; all textures/sprites/audio procedurally generated.

## Decisions
- Vanilla ES modules, static `index.html` + `styles.css` + `js/*.js`; no build step.
- Custom Canvas 2D software raycaster (PS1/Silent Hill style) rather than Three.js; target pixel buffer ~240k px desktop / ~128k mobile.
- Core loop: 3 sigils, one exit gate; monster freezes while in view/LOS, advances when unseen; staring raises “gaze” meter, fractures reality at 100% (3 reality points); fractures teleport monster closer; 0 reality = death.
- Reality break visuals: buffer tearing, CSS fracture animation, red edge glow, whispers, shake.
- Audio fully synthesized with WebAudio (drone, heartbeat, whispers, footsteps, sigils, fracture, death, win).
- Mobile: floating left-half joystick, right-half drag look, LISTEN button, pause under coarse-pointer media.
- Performance: removed expensive CSS canvas `filter` and continuous transform; removed animated grain/scanline overlays; baked grain + scanlines into renderer buffer; static vignette retained.
- Menu uses the live 3D scene as background with large serif typography.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/maze.js`, `js/textures.js`, `js/renderer.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/game.js`.
- Maze generation, braiding, BFS pathfinding, LOS checks, sigil/exit/monster placement.
- Renderer: DDA walls, textured floor/ceiling, z-buffered billboards, flashlight cone, portal/sigil/watcher glows, buffer grain+scanlines, fracture tear bands.
- Gameplay: movement/collision, pointer-lock + drag look, touch controls, freeze/gaze/fracture/reality/death/win, listen compass, HUD, menus, settings persistence.
- Audio engine with ambient, heartbeat, whispers, monster presence, stingers.
- Performance optimized to ~60 fps steady after startup in Xvfb/software Chromium (renderer ~7 ms).
- Pointer-lock spin fix: `lockGrace` 320 ms and ignores |movement| > 160 to prevent synthetic-click camera spin in capture.
- Desktop/mobile menu and gameplay screenshots verified; HUD pause button overlap fixed (hidden outside coarse pointer).

### Active
- Visual polish iteration, specifically:
  - Portal sprite looks too neon/ladder-like; inner horizontal bars and rectangular glow need redesign (arch outline + faint inner light).
  - Monster face improved but still reads slightly mask-like; scream pose triggers at distance < 2.8 and should likely be lowered to ~1.9.
  - Jumpscare image bug: screenshot shows mostly static noise with only a tiny sliver at top.
- Jumpscare debug: image loads (`naturalWidth 240`, `naturalHeight 504`, rect `x≈360, y≈-325, w≈718, h≈1508`), element visible/active, but monster image not visible — likely z-order/opacity interaction with `.jumpscare-static` or image content/visibility.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix jumpscare: inspect/repair `.jumpscare img` composition (likely static overlay `mix-blend-mode: screen` + noisy background washing it out, or image layer stacking/opacity); screenshot at ~250 ms and ~1 s to verify monster fills screen.
2. Redesign `portalSprite()` in `js/textures.js` (remove horizontal ladder bars / rectangular inner fill; keep luminous arch, add soft interior glow/particles); reduce glow sprite brightness/size if needed.
3. Change scream pose threshold in `js/game.js` from `< 2.8` to ~`< 1.9` (or boost-only) and refine monster face/eyes to be less cartoonish; maybe soften watcher eyes further.
4. Re-run screenshots/automated checks: menu, gameplay, monster mid/close, sigil, portal locked/open, gaze high, fracture, jumpscare, death card, win card; desktop + mobile (with `isMobile/hasTouch`).
5. Add/verify gameplay automation: sigil collection, exit lock/open, monster catch, gaze fracture, restart flow; ensure no page/console errors.
6. Final performance check (steady ~60 fps) and mobile layout (390x844, safe areas, touch buttons).
7. Commit changes only if requested.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: game state, input, loop, monster/gaze/fracture/death/win, debug API `window.__DLB`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/renderer.js`: raycaster, floor/ceiling, sprites, grain/scanlines/tear effects.
